output.brief:
Store 14's rise is not yet shown to be a real increase in losses. The Q1–Q3 numbers are estimates extrapolated from partial cycle counts. Back-testing shows they can be off by about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across the chain, about half of the stores with two consecutive rises like this were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full-count shrink was 1.5–1.8% for the last three years. The rise in recorded shoplifting incidents looks mostly like a reporting effect: the incident app launched chain-wide on 1 April, and incident counts rose across the chain while chain shrink stayed flat. The night-stocker tip was checked against CCTV and not substantiated. Sales mix did not change, so mix does not explain it. Self-checkout and customer theft remain possible but unproven. Neighbouring stores without self-checkout are flat or falling, which fits either self-checkout or noise.

What to do: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject the proposal to skip it, because skipping it removes the only reliable measurement. Hold off on a guard, on pulling or staffing the lanes, and on any action against the stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. If the count confirms a real rise, investigate the self-checkout lanes and customer theft then. Confidence is moderate on the causes and high on keeping the count.
